# Fixed or Variable — video

A 100-second summary of the [Fixed or Variable
article](/finance/fixed-or-variable.md), built with
[HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) (`npx hyperframes`). Kinetic type
and data in Collegica's own palette — no generated imagery, renders locally for
free. Same approach as the [`ai-planning`](https://github.com/Collegica/collegica/tree/main/video/ai-planning),
[`next-job`](https://github.com/Collegica/collegica/tree/main/video/next-job) and
[`budget-from-statements`](https://github.com/Collegica/collegica/tree/main/video/budget-from-statements) videos; read any
of those READMEs for the full rationale (Kokoro TTS setup, the render/check
loop). This one only notes what differs.

## Rebuild

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate   # first time only
pip install kokoro-onnx soundfile                     # first time only
npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.33 check
npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.33 render -o _output/fixed-or-variable.mp4 --crf 23 --low-memory-mode
cp _output/fixed-or-variable.mp4 ../../website/static/video/finance/fixed-or-variable.mp4
```

**`--low-memory-mode` is required here.** At 100 seconds this is the longest of
the four videos, and the default render path overran the free disk on this
machine with temporary frames. What the flag actually does, per `render
--help`: the *safe profile* — one worker, screenshot capture, no worker
calibration, on by default on machines with 8 GB or less. With it, 3,013
frames rendered in 2 min 10 s (measured 2026-09-13). If the real problem is
a small temp partition, `--frames-cache-dir` relocates the frame cache.

## Structure

- `index.html` — master timeline, 7 frames, hard cuts with a 0.35s crossfade.
  Total 100.41s.
- `compositions/frames/0N-*.html`:
  1. **hook** — the two stock answers, struck through
  2. **rate-path** — the overnight rate drawn 2021→2026, stroke-dashoffset
  3. **2021** — 1.69% fixed vs 0.98% variable, verdict counting up to $48,935
  4. **trigger** — a fixed payment filling with interest until it overflows,
     ending on $478,848 still owing
  5. **2023** — the same layout, the opposite verdict
  6. **crossover** — twelve signing dates, teal above the line and amber below
  7. **close** — three better questions, and the URL
- `assets/fixed-or-variable-hero.jpg` — the article's hero, kept for reference;
  no composition currently draws it (the video is type and data throughout).
- `audio/` — narration WAVs, Kokoro `af_heart`, one per frame.

## Numbers on screen

Every figure is generated by the article's own simulator
(`website/static/js/fixed-or-variable/mortgage.js`) and sourced in
[`docs/research/2026-09-10-fixed-or-variable/`](../../docs/research/2026-09-10-fixed-or-variable/).
Two things are worth knowing if you edit a frame:

- **Frame 2's polyline is the real overnight path**, generated from
  `rates.json` rather than drawn by eye. Regenerate it from that file if the
  rate history changes; do not nudge points to look better.
- **Frame 6's bar widths are proportional to the real interest margins**, scaled
  so the largest ($48,935, September 2021) is 100%. The smallest (June 2023,
  $730) is floored at 2.5% so it stays visible — the only deliberate
  departure from proportionality, and it makes that bar look larger than it is
  rather than smaller.

Same pronunciation note as the other three videos: frame 7's TTS input spells
"Collegica" as "College-ika" so Kokoro reads it correctly; the on-screen text
and URL stay spelled properly.
